issues.description: Field Farm.animals: the problem statement (UML and task text) specifies that the farm's animals collection must be a List<Animal> and that an ArrayList should be initialized in the no-arg constructor. The solution implementation declares the field as private Set<Animal> animals and initializes it with new HashSet<>() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 9-13). This divergence between the specified attribute type (List/ArrayList) and the solution (Set/HashSet) can confuse students about which collection type to implement and may cause tests or guidance that expect List semantics to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent. Preferred fix: change the solution to use List<Animal> for the animals field, import java.util.List and java.util.ArrayList, and initialize animals = new ArrayList<>(); in the no-arg constructor. Update getter/setter signatures to return/accept List<Animal> and keep addAnimal(Animal) logic unchanged. Alternatively (less preferred), update the problem statement and template to explicitly allow a Set/HashSet and remove the ArrayList requirement — but ensure all artifacts (problem statement, template, solution, and tests) consistently specify the same collection type.
